analysis.title: Liquid Insight: Rate shock unlikely over
key_insights: BofA still expects modestly higher US front-end rates and forecasts the 2Y yield at 5% by end-2026. It holds a US 2s30s curve flattening trade and recommends an underweight US front-end bias.
The underweight rests on three points: US rates are not materially restricting activity, Fed pricing can rise further, and commodity risks skew to the upside.

On restrictiveness, 3m annualized core CPI and the Bloomberg labor surprise index are at their highest levels since 1H-2024, before the first Fed cuts. Neither credit spreads nor loan growth have tightened or slowed meaningfully.
Higher rates have stopped loan growth from accelerating but have not yet slowed it. Investors in BofA's FX and Rates Sentiment Survey see US monetary policy as accommodative.
Fed pricing can stretch further. BofA's preferred Taylor rule metric puts fed funds near or above 5% today. The BofA US economics team added another Fed hike to its path last week.
BofA does not rule out a 50bp Fed hike in December. It becomes more likely if November unemployment reaches 4.0%, November average hourly earnings rise 0.4% m/m, and tech sentiment stabilizes.

BofA argues against client pushback that a 50bp hike would imply the October hold was a mistake: its view is that it is better to address mistakes early. It also expects Fed Chair Warsh to sound hawkish at his next policy remarks.

Oil is priced close to the BofA commodity team's forecasts and the market looks optimistic on Hormuz normalization. Any US-Iran escalation would be upside for oil and rates. Clients see demand destruction only above $125 oil.

Positioning leans toward steepeners across US futures proxies, active fund betas and survey responses. A continued repricing higher in the US front end would drag all tenors up and flatten curves, which BofA calls the likely global duration pain trade.

Highest-conviction US macro rates expression is the 2s30s flattener: entry 62bp, target 40bp, current 64bp, stop 100bp. BofA was stopped out of its pay 2Y position about 1.5 weeks ago and missed a large front-end rate rise.

For investors who want to be long duration, BofA recommends conditional structures: long 1y10y receiver spreads or 15m5y vs 3m5y receiver calendars. In Europe it recommends receiving 2y1y OIS, citing limited cut pricing despite energy shock and tight financial conditions.
Outside the US, the BofA global rates team has a bullish and flattening curve bias in most regions.

charts_described: Exhibit 1 plots 2Y and 10Y yield changes against y/y loan growth, captioned: higher rates have stopped loan growth pace from rising but not yet cooling it.
Exhibit 2 plots 3m annualized core CPI and core PCE, captioned: recent inflation measures are moving wrong way for Fed.
Exhibit 3 plots the Bloomberg labor surprise index against the US 2Y yield, captioned: labor surprises have improved, pulling 2Y yields higher.
Exhibit 4 plots the US 10Y yield against the investment grade option adjusted spread, captioned: rates have risen but credit spreads have not materially widened.
Exhibit 5 shows survey responses on the current stance of US monetary policy, captioned: investors see US monetary policy stance as accommodative.
Exhibit 6 plots the Taylor rule against the Fed target, captioned: Taylor Rule is running well above target.

Exhibit 7 shows survey responses on the oil price and duration that would trigger a sharp consumer slowdown, captioned: oil of 125-150$/bbl for more than 3 months would trigger it according to a plurality of investors.
Exhibit 8 shows futures positioning proxies by contract, captioned: futures proxy implies curve to twist flatten.
Exhibit 9 shows PCA-regression curve betas, captioned: betas suggest funds are likely positioning for steepeners.
vol_and_positioning: Futures positioning proxies show a long bias at the front end and a short bias at the long end, which implies heavy steepener positioning and a bias for the curve to twist flatter.
Active fund curve betas from PCA regression suggest funds are positioned for steepeners versus benchmark.
Survey responses indicate clients are positioned globally in steepeners. BofA says a flatter, higher-rate move may be the global duration pain trade.
Receiver calendars are vega weighted. BofA points to its US vol note, 'A higher regime in '27', for the vol view.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict and Hormuz normalization: markets price high odds of the status quo, and escalation would lift oil and rates.

tension_points.bull_case: Oil markets look optimistic with high odds of status quo and Hormuz normalization, and oil is priced close to the BofA commodity team forecasts.
tension_points.bear_case: Any escalation in the US-Iran conflict could lift oil and rates. Higher oil can cool demand, but clients do not see demand destruction below $125.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Oil above $125 sustained would start to cause demand destruction, per the BofA sentiment survey, and would cap further rate upside.

tension_points.theme: US curve flattener vs steepener positioning
tension_points.bull_case: Heavy client positioning in steepeners means a repricing higher in the US front end would flatten the curve, which BofA calls the global duration pain trade.
tension_points.bear_case: Frontloaded cuts plus a hawkish Fed shift in the medium term would hurt receiver structures for those wanting to be long duration.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The 2s30s flattener has a stop at 100bp from a current 64bp.

theme_stances.key_argument: US rates are not materially restricting activity, Fed pricing has catching up to do, and commodity risks skew up.
theme_stances.evidence: We still expect modestly higher US front end rates.

theme_stances.key_argument: Addressing policy mistakes early is better than letting them grow larger.
